title: Libanius, Declamations (Μελέται), 51 pieces; unit = those absent from the Russian, English and German selections / Либаний, Декламации
author: Libanius of Antioch
size: 51 declamations in Foerster vols. V–VII (three Teubner volumes); several hundred thousand words (estimate)
edition: Foerster, Libanii opera V–VII (Teubner 1909–13), public domain; scans on archive.org.
ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Либаний': Decl. 1 (Raytsina 1997) and Decl. 26, 28, 29 (Grabar-Passek 1961/1964) only.
en_evidence: D. A. Russell, Libanius: Imaginary Speeches, a selection (1996), per German Wikipedia and BMCR 2013.02.38. No complete English found.
other_translations: German: U. Lempp, Libanios: Musterreden (2015), scope unverified. Other single pieces may exist.
value: The largest Greek declamation corpus: classical Athens, Homer and New Comedy re-performed in a 4th-century school. Key for education, reception of Demosthenes and Socrates, and the Byzantine rhetorical canon.
ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Long and rhetorically regular Attic prose; stasis structure helps alignment. Requires checking for overlap with Russell and Lempp first.
pilot_unit: One historical declamation not in Russell or Lempp (to be chosen after checking their contents), about 8,000–10,000 words.
